"u seem overly focused on habits/way of operating/principles/thinking shit out" -- this was a reply somewhere, I can't find it

but I'd clarify it as follows...risk vs autopilot, like Buffett eating at same restaurant each day (in QT)

I'm receptive to the feedback bc there's definitely some "guy" u dont wanna be here

the goal isnt to have every free minute of ur day nailed down with busy meetings/calls...this is straight goober behavior, Doorknob guy, "step counter" guy

not as bad as Bookmark Guy, but pretty close, like whatever that corner of twtr is with all the weird performative self-help grind LARP

where theres a photo of a full calendar next to three Bloomberg terminal screens, one with every Maersk VLCC on the planet, one with BRLJPY and the other with some neon-colored MC Escher looking option volatility surface

like bro no possible job exists where u are doing all three of those things, I'm sorry

the goal, really, is that u want large blocks of unstructured time on ur calendar so u can think, read, and write...buffett's day is basically 50% reading and 50% talking to very tight inner circle

this is how it should be if u take risk for a living/in a "performance" role where outcomes justify process

have to unwire and rewire a lot of shit, like, it doesnt matter if u only work 1 minute a day, or only make 1 decision per year and not 1000

u optimize for whatever gets u to flawless execution, not "busywork"

I didnt understand most of this until mid 30s and am still rearranging a lot of it. basically, nobody gives a fuck how hard u work, u have to remove that and any/all "optics" as inputs.

u either get the job done, or u dont...period

so imo all the shit like sleep, diet, exercise, u want that nailed to the wall. less things to think about.

same for how u think abt relationships both old and new, how u think about the crowd, society, the way u interact with the world, how u think about being of service, ur "circle of competence"...all these habits and filtering mechanisms that comprise ur worldview.

these practices should be lifelong, u only need to get them right once, then u upload/install them and ur good from age 40 to age 100

eat the same shit, wear the same shit, same lifting schedule, same sleep schedule

autopilot all that

life is variable and fortune is a fickle mistress, having this stuff hardcoded ensures u stay grounded + keeps ur head about u in chaos

plus makes it much much easier to rebound from adversity and setbacks, bc u know that good or bad, ur life really doesnt change that much

all ur processes are in place + u have (hopefully) thought thru all the shit that could go wrong in advance, vs trying to fix the plane mid-flight

so its not about "be overly rigid/rules-based in absolutely everything," mostly life doesnt work like that. its closer to "control what you can control"

study how seneca/plutarch impart wisdom and you'll see it, a combo of precepts reinforced by stories + moral lessons, this isnt really a new way of operating

those precepts are ur weapons, ur guideposts, that should steer u through whatever uncertainty u go through...or at the very least, prevent u from flying right the fuck off Rainbow Road.
